s: Six links: two on the internet, four into a radio
t: Entry: Settings → Server . The page holds the two internet servers only, one card each, each with its own switch. The address and credentials live one level down. Link Carries RX TX APRS-IS TCP over t
The two internet links are peers, and APRS-IS gets no special status. Its parameters live on its own sub-page, separate from the APRSNETCN card. Settings → Server → APRS-IS server : enter the address

APRSNETCN stands beside APRS-IS. It speaks the same APRS-IS protocol, the server sits in China, and the address is yours to fill in. It can carry both directions, and it can be the only link online. S

Settings → Beacon → Enable position beacon (on by default). Interval defaults to 60 s — APRS-IS asks mobiles not to go below 60 s; the hard minimum is 5 s (smaller values are rejected by validation).

Item-by-item reference: name, control, default, description — generated from the code and the official strings, so it stays in sync.

Settings # Station, location, links data The Settings page opens with eight category cards (each leading to its own page) plus eleven direct entries. Below, every setting is listed: name, control, def
Station # Callsign · SSID · Symbol Identity is the root of every frame: the callsign must match your licence, and the SSID states the station type (-9 mobile, -7 handheld are common). Setting Control

Servers # Two links · filter range One card per server; the address and credentials live one level down. This page keeps the receive range and a callsign filter. Changes apply only with “Save apply”.

APRS-IS server # Address, port and passcode go here. One APRS-IS link: address, port, Passcode and an optional WebSocket URL. An empty address connects nothing; no server is preset. APRS-IS connection

APRSNETCN SERVER # A server built on the APRSNETCN SERVER protocol. It carries traffic both ways. APRSNETCN stands beside APRS-IS. Address and port go here, then the account and Passcode. Both servers
